title: Ye Wretched, Hungry, Starving Poor
description: Ye Wretched, Hungry, Starving Poor in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 266 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Invitation to the Gospel Feast”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ye wret-ched, hun-gry, starv-ing poor, Be-hold a roy-al feast, Where mer-cy spreads her boun-teous store, For ev-ery hum-ble guest!

lines: Ye wretched, hungry, starving poor,
Behold a royal feast,
Where mercy spreads her bounteous store,
For every humble guest!
See, Jesus stands with open arms!
He calls, he bids you come; —
Guilt holds you back, and fear alarms, —
But see, there yet is room!
Come then, and with his people taste
The blessings of his love;
While hope attends the sweet repast,
Of nobler joys above.
There, with united heart and voice,
Before the eternal throne,
Ten thousand thousand souls rejoice
In ecstasies unknown.
And yet ten thousand thousand more
Are welcome still to come:
Ye longing souls, the grace adore; —
Approach, there yet is room.

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
